standard.title: Generate and communicate design ideas
standard.description: generate and communicate design ideas and decisions using appropriate attributions, technical terms and graphical representation techniques, including using digital tools
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can generate and communicate design ideas through describing, drawing or modelling, including using digital tools (AC9TDE2P01). They have communicated design ideas informally. They have not yet used technical terms, annotated diagrams, attributions, or more formal graphical representation techniques.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students generate and communicate design ideas and decisions using appropriate technical terms, attributions and graphical representation techniques, including annotated diagrams and digital tools.

nodes.label: Generating design ideas through sketching and modelling
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce multiple design ideas for a problem using thumbnail sketches or models
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least two thumbnail sketches or models for a design problem, with enough detail to distinguish the ideas
nodes.typical_width: Produce multiple thumbnail sketches, labelled drawings and/or models for design problems; include features and modifications in each idea; explore ideas for different design problems
wider: Generate design ideas inspired by First Nations Australians' watercraft or other traditional designs — describe how prior design knowledge can inform new ideas

Generate design ideas for solutions using Safety by Design principles — produce sketches that show how the design ensures accessibility for all users (e.g. all parents and carers can access communication)
success_criteria: Produces at least two visibly different design ideas
Each sketch or model shows enough detail to understand what it proposes
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who produce only one design idea arrive at N2 and N3 with nothing to annotate or communicate distinctively — the communication tasks assume multiple ideas have been generated.

nodes.label: Using technical terms and annotations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can label a design drawing using appropriate technical terms and explain what each component is and does
nodes.minimum_width: Label at least one design drawing with technical terms for two or more components, with a brief explanation of each
nodes.typical_width: Communicate design ideas using annotated diagrams with technical terms for all major components; include labels and descriptions explaining materials used, their properties, and the intended function of components or the whole system
wider: Annotate a design for a more complex system (e.g. a pushcart with chassis, axle, wheels and steering) using technical terms for each component — explain not just what each part is but why it was designed that way

Research and apply technical terms from a related design field (e.g. engineering, textile design) to annotate a student design — discuss how technical language helps communicate design decisions to different audiences

response_modes.reason: Technical vocabulary in design communication needs fluency — students who can label a design correctly and consistently are better positioned for the more complex communication tasks in subsequent years. Precision and accuracy in annotation matters more than breadth of context here.

success_criteria: Uses at least two technical terms correctly in annotations
Annotations explain function, not just name the part
nodes.hinge_reason: Technical annotation and attributions are required components of the N3 digital communication task — students who have not consolidated annotation practice cannot produce the complete communication the descriptor requires.

nodes.label: Communicating and sharing design ideas with attributions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share and document design ideas using digital tools, including appropriate attributions and privacy considerations
nodes.minimum_width: Share a design idea using a digital tool, with at least one attribution for an idea or reference that informed it
nodes.typical_width: Plan, share and document creative design ideas using digital tools; apply appropriate technical terms; include attributions for ideas drawn from other sources; apply privacy considerations when sharing collaboratively (e.g. class blog, shared document)
wider: Document a design process using a class blog or collaborative digital document — include annotations, attributions and reflections on design decisions shared selectively with peers
Communicate a design idea for a cultural context beyond the student's own experience — discuss what additional research and attribution is needed to communicate the design respectfully and accurately

response_modes.reason: Communicating a complete design idea using digital tools, technical terms, annotations and attributions together is the integration point. Each element has been practised separately — this node is where students coordinate them into a coherent design communication.

success_criteria: Design communication includes technical terms and at least one attribution
Digital tool has been used to share or document the design
